speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; to help you, I need to ask a few questions. Is this rash present at birth, or did it appear after you were born?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. You mentioned the rash appeared on day 4; is it associated with any blisters, pustules, or crusting on the skin?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Varicella (Chickenpox). The presentation of a generalized maculopapular rash with pustules on an erythematous base, sparing the palms and soles, appearing on day 4 of life in an infant born to a mother with no prenatal care (potentially allowing maternal immunity to wane or insufficient transfer) is classic for neonatal varicella. REQUEST TEST: Maternal Varicella_Zoster_IgG titer. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Clinical_Photograph_Rash_Distribution.
